title: The Terracotta Army Mausoleum
synopsis: Learn about the mausoleum guarded by the Terracotta Army.

fullText.simplified:
兵马俑守护的陵墓

    说起兵马俑，大家都并不陌生。但是相对于兵马俑来说，人们对它们所守护的陵墓则陌生许多。事实上，兵马俑只是秦始皇的“手办”，是秦始皇陵的守卫者。这座气势恢宏的陵墓主体并没有进行大规模考古发掘，我们所见的兵马俑只是其冰山一角。
    作为首位统一中国并创造皇帝这一称呼的人，野心勃勃的秦始皇对长生不老的追求可谓空前执着。除了在全国各地寻求长生不老的灵丹妙药以外，他还在生前就开始着手陵墓的修建工程。这一工程共耗时39年，直到秦始皇去世的第二年才全部完工，前后动用人数达70余万之巨。整个陵墓从内到外分别是地宫、封土堆、兵马俑坑和其他陵园建筑。总占地面积56.25平方公里，相当于78个故宫或者两个澳门。
    而更令人震惊的是秦始皇陵的设计思路——事死如事生。即把活人的生活方式复制到死后的世界中去，兵马俑就是埋在秦陵地宫外侧的护卫军，这七千名战士将在另一世界继续保卫秦始皇陵的核心——地宫。秦陵地宫占地面积为五个标准足球场大小，围绕着这座神秘地宫的传说不胜枚举。据传说秦始皇让工匠们利用大量水银模拟了名山大川，还原了黄河、长江、淮河等水系，也就是说秦始皇在他的陵墓里创造了一个微缩版的中国！
    在本世纪初进行的一次大规模科考项目中，考古学家利用地质勘测、红外遥感等技术手段对秦陵地宫进行了深入研究。研究显示，地宫上方的封土堆汞含量严重超标，且呈现规律的形状分布，在这些形状上有一个物体在不停移动。根据这一发现，考古学家们推断，秦陵地宫至今保存完整，且水银河流这一传说是真实可信的。而这一不断移动的物体很可能就是漂浮在水银上的秦始皇的棺椁。据相关史籍记载，秦陵地宫上具天文、下具地理。也就是说，地宫上方应该还有星宿图，据传说是用名贵的夜明珠镶嵌而成的。但这一点目前科考工作还无法证实。就目前了解信息来看，秦始皇当年在死后继续云游四海、俯察地理、统治秦国的愿望在陵墓设计中是实现了的。
    受目前技术所限，由于秦陵地宫面积过大，无法规避地宫打开后迅速氧化的问题，秦陵地宫仍然未进行发掘。留给我们的仍然是无数秘密和猜测，而谜底只能交由后人揭晓了。
fullText.traditional:
兵馬俑守護的陵墓

    說起兵馬俑，大家都並不陌生。但是相對於兵馬俑來說，人們對它們所守護的陵墓則陌生許多。事實上，兵馬俑只是秦始皇的“手辦”，是秦始皇陵的守衛者。這座氣勢恢宏的陵墓主體並沒有進行大規模考古發掘，我們所見的兵馬俑只是其冰山一角。
    作為首位統一中國並創造皇帝這一稱呼的人，野心勃勃的秦始皇對長生不老的追求可謂空前執著。除了在全國各地尋求長生不老的靈丹妙藥以外，他還在生前就開始著手陵墓的修建工程。這一工程共耗時39年，直到秦始皇去世的第二年才全部完工，前後動用人數達70餘萬之巨。整個陵墓從內到外分別是地宮、封土堆、兵馬俑坑和其他陵園建築。總占地面積56.25平方公里，相當於78個故宮或者兩個澳門。
    而更令人震驚的是秦始皇陵的設計思路——事死如事生。即把活人的生活方式複製到死後的世界中去，兵馬俑就是埋在秦陵地宮外側的護衛軍，這七千名戰士將在另一世界繼續保衛秦始皇陵的核心——地宮。秦陵地宮占地面積為五個標準足球場大小，圍繞著這座神秘地宮的傳說不勝枚舉。據傳說秦始皇讓工匠們利用大量水銀模擬了名山大川，還原了黃河、長江、淮河等水系，也就是說秦始皇在他的陵墓裡創造了一個微縮版的中國！
    在本世紀初進行的一次大規模科考項目中，考古學家利用地質勘測、紅外遙感等技術手段對秦陵地宮進行了深入研究。研究顯示，地宮上方的封土堆汞含量嚴重超標，且呈現規律的形狀分佈，在這些形狀上有一個物體在不停移動。根據這一發現，考古學家們推斷，秦陵地宮至今保存完整，且水銀河流這一傳說是真實可信的。而這一不斷移動的物體很可能就是漂浮在水銀上的秦始皇的棺槨。據相關史籍記載，秦陵地宮上具天文、下具地理。也就是說，地宮上方應該還有星宿圖，據傳說是用名貴的夜明珠鑲嵌而成的。但這一點目前科考工作還無法證實。就目前了解信息來看，秦始皇當年在死後繼續雲遊四海、俯察地理、統治秦國的願望在陵墓設計中是實現了的。
    受目前技術所限，由於秦陵地宮面積過大，無法規避地宮打開後迅速氧化的問題，秦陵地宮仍然未進行發掘。留給我們的仍然是無數秘密和猜測，而謎底只能交由後人揭曉了。

sentences.simplified: 但这一点目前科考工作还无法证实。
sentences.traditional: 但這一點目前科考工作還無法證實。
sentences.pinyin: dàn zhè yì diǎn mù qián kē kǎo gōng zuò hái wú fǎ zhèng shí
sentences.english: According to legend, they are made of embedded precious luminous pearls.

sentences.simplified: 就目前了解信息来看，
sentences.traditional: 就目前了解信息來看，
sentences.pinyin: jiù mù qián liǎo jiě xìn xī lái kàn
sentences.english: But as of now, this has not yet been proven by scientific investigation.

sentences.simplified: 秦始皇当年在死后继续云游四海、俯察地理、统治秦国的愿望
sentences.traditional: 秦始皇當年在死後繼續雲遊四海、俯察地理、統治秦國的願望
sentences.pinyin: qín shǐ huáng dāng nián zài sǐ hòu jì xù yún yóu sì hǎi fǔ chá dì lǐ tǒng zhì qín guó de yuàn wàng
sentences.english: From the information we currently have, ..

sentences.simplified: 在陵墓设计中是实现了的。
sentences.traditional: 在陵墓設計中是實現了的。
sentences.pinyin: zài líng mù shè jì zhōng shì shí xiàn le de
sentences.english: .. the desires of Qin Shi Huang to continue to travel the country, survey the geography, and rule over the State of Qin after his death,

.. were realized in the design of the mausoleum.
.

sentences.simplified: 受目前技术所限，
sentences.traditional: 受目前技術所限，
sentences.pinyin: shòu mù qián jì shù suǒ xiàn

sentences.simplified: 由于秦陵地宫面积过大，
sentences.traditional: 由於秦陵地宮面積過大，
sentences.pinyin: yóu yú qín líng dì gōng miàn jī guò dà
sentences.english: With the limitations of current technology, ..

sentences.simplified: 无法规避地宫打开后迅速氧化的问题，
sentences.traditional: 無法規避地宮打開後迅速氧化的問題，
sentences.pinyin: wú fǎ guī bì dì gōng dǎ kāi hòu xùn sù yǎng huà de wèn tí
sentences.english: .. because the underground palace of the Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor is too large in area, ..

sentences.simplified: 秦陵地宫仍然未进行发掘。
sentences.traditional: 秦陵地宮仍然未進行發掘。
sentences.pinyin: qín líng dì gōng réng rán wèi jìn xíng fā jué
sentences.english: .. there is no way to avoid the problem of rapid oxidation once the underground palace is opened.

sentences.simplified: 留给我们的仍然是无数秘密和猜测，
sentences.traditional: 留給我們的仍然是無數秘密和猜測，
sentences.pinyin: liú gěi wǒ men de réng rán shì wú shù mì mì hé cāi cè
sentences.english: So, the underground palace of the Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor has yet to be excavated.

sentences.simplified: 而谜底只能交由后人揭晓了。
sentences.traditional: 而謎底只能交由後人揭曉了。
sentences.pinyin: ér mí dǐ zhǐ néng jiāo yóu hòu rén jiē xiǎo le
sentences.english: What we are left with is endless secrets and conjectures, ..
.. the answers to which we can only leave for future generations to uncover.

raw.synopsis: Learn about the mausoleum guarded by the Terracotta Army.
sentence_translations: The Mausoleum Guarded by the Terracotta Army
Everyone is familiar with the Terracotta Warriors.
But compared to the Terracotta Warriors, people are much less familiar with the mausoleum that they guard.
In reality, the Terracotta Warriors are just Qin Shi Huang’s “action figures”.
They are the guards of the Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor.
There has been no large scale archeological excavation of the main part of this vast and imposing mausoleum.
The Terracotta Warriors that we see are just the tip of the iceberg.
As the first person to unite China and create the title of emperor, ..
.. Qin Shi Huang, who was consumed with ambition, pursued immortality with what can be described as unprecedented persistence.
Besides seeking the elixir of life from all across China, he also began work on the construction of his mausoleum while still living.
This project took a total of 39 years and was only finished in the second year after Qin Shi Huang’s death.
From beginning to end, more than 700,000 people were involved in its construction.
From the inside to the outside, the mausoleum is divided into ..
.. the underground palace, the grave mound, the pits of the terracotta warriors, and other mausoleum constructions.
The total area is 56.25 square kilometers, the equivalent of 78 Forbidden Cities, or two Macaus.
Yet even more astonishing is the thought process behind the design of the Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor, ..
..  serving the dead as if they were alive.
That is, the way of life of the living was replicated in the world after death.
The Terracotta Warriors are guards buried in the outer areas of the underground palace in the Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor.
In the next world, these 7,000 fighters continue to protect the core of the Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor, the underground palace.
The underground palace has a total area of five standard soccer fields.
The legends surrounding this mysterious underground palace are innumerable.
According to legend, Qin Shi Huang had craftsmen use large amounts of mercury to simulate famous mountains and great rivers.
He recreated river systems such as the Yellow River, the Yangtze River, and the Huai River.
Essentially, Qin Shi Huang created a miniature version of China in his mausoleum!
During a large scale research project conducted at the beginning of this century, ..
.. archaeologists used techniques such as geological surveying and infrared remote sensing ..
.. to conduct in-depth research on the underground palace.
The research showed that the grave mound located above the underground palace contained significantly elevated levels of mercury.
In addition, the spatial distribution of mercury showed a regular pattern, with a constantly moving object on top of these shapes.
On the basis of this discovery, the archaeologists inferred that the underground palace is still completely intact.
In addition, the legend of the mercury rivers is true.
This continuously moving object is very likely to be Qin Shi Huang’s coffin, floating on the mercury.
According to related historical records, ..
.. the underground palace of the Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor has astronomy on top and geography on the bottom.
In other words, there should be constellation charts at the top of the underground palace.
According to legend, they are made of embedded precious luminous pearls.
But as of now, this has not yet been proven by scientific investigation.
From the information we currently have, ..
.. the desires of Qin Shi Huang to continue to travel the country, survey the geography, and rule over the State of Qin after his death,

.. were realized in the design of the mausoleum.
.
With the limitations of current technology, ..
.. because the underground palace of the Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor is too large in area, ..
.. there is no way to avoid the problem of rapid oxidation once the underground palace is opened.
So, the underground palace of the Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor has yet to be excavated.
What we are left with is endless secrets and conjectures, ..
.. the answers to which we can only leave for future generations to uncover.
